posts.text:
11 venutres.

4 countries.

54 companies featured so far this year.

But that is not the interesting part.

The interesting part is what founders are choosing to build before the rest of the market notices.

Inside the 3rd Frontier Deal Flow cohort, you will find companies like

Soterya, Inc., Arzya Principle Knowledge Advisory, and companies working on:

▪️ AI infrastructure for industries still running on spreadsheets

▪️ Robotics tackling problems humans were never meant to do manually

▪️ Healthcare platforms attacking bottlenecks that cost lives and billions

▪️ Defense technologies built for a very different geopolitical decade

▪️ Advanced manufacturing systems designed for a world rebuilding supply chains

▪️ Digital infrastructure for the next generation of global businesses

A few patterns stood out:

→ Pre-Seed continues to dominate the pipeline.

→ AI remains powerful, but no longer wins attention on its own.

→ The strongest companies are solving physical-world problems, not just digital ones.

→ Geography matters less than it used to. Signal is becoming global.

In the full 22nd Century Frontier report you'll find answers to questions like:

❓ Which sectors are attracting the strongest founder activity right now?

❓ Where is frontier innovation emerging geographically?

❓ What does the current early-stage market actually look like beneath the headlines?

❓ Which themes are investors likely to spend the next 12-24 months chasing?

❓ What separates companies that get attention from companies that get funded?

250+ Unicorn Pitch Decks. The presentations behind $100B+ raised

We've put together a database of 250+ fundraising decks from some of the world's most successful startups, including:

See how category-defining companies told their story, structured their decks, and convinced investors to back them.

Whether you're building your first pitch deck or preparing for your next round, there's no better way to learn than from companies that have already done it.

👇 Comment "DECK" and I'll send you the collection 👇

🚀 Buffett’s Secret Weapons: Competence & Patience 🚀

Warren Buffett reminds us that in investing...

and in business...

two principles stand above all:

• 𝐂𝐢𝐫𝐜𝐥𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐞𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞:

Play where you have expertise. 

Deep knowledge compounds returns and reduces avoidable risks.

• 𝐏𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞:

Great opportunities often require waiting for the right moment. 

Impulse decisions erode long-term value.

𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐛𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐦𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐢𝐬 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐬 𝐥𝐞𝐠𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐞𝐬.

🎥 (Watch the clip - Buffett’s timeless advice for leaders)

——————

♻ Useful for your network too? Repost
🔔 Want to see more? Follow 👨‍💻 Petar Dimov 🔥

𝐒𝐭𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐢𝐬𝐧’𝐭 𝐚 𝐬𝐢𝐠𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐞.

𝐈𝐭’𝐬 𝐚 𝐬𝐢𝐠𝐧 𝐲𝐨𝐮’𝐫𝐞 𝐚𝐯𝐨𝐢𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧.

Jeff Bezos said it well: 

Stress doesn’t come from challenges themselves.

It comes from knowing there’s something you should do… 

and not doing it.

In leadership, that’s often the gap:

Not a lack of insight...

but a lack of 𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 on the things we already understand.

Here’s what I’ve seen among strong leaders:

 • 𝐃𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧

They make the tough call before it becomes a crisis.

 • 𝐃𝐢𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

They confront issues early, not emotionally, but clearly.

 • 𝐄𝐱𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

They take the next step, even if it’s uncomfortable.

Stress shrinks the moment you move.

Even a small step resets your mind and your momentum.

If something is weighing on you today, address it.

Not perfectly

just honestly.

That’s where relief starts.

♻️ Repost to keep your network informed.
🔔 Follow (Petar Dimov 🔥) for more.

video source: social media

A founder can have a great product, real traction, and a huge market...

...and still lose the room in the first five minutes.

Why?

Because investors don't invest in slides.

They invest in stories they can believe.

A few ideas from our latest piece:

▪️ The best pitches don't start with the product. 

They start with a problem that feels impossible to ignore.

▪️ Investors remember narratives, not feature lists.

▪️ Every great deck follows a hidden structure:

World → Pain → Change → Solution → Proof → Future.

▪️ Traction is where the story stops being theoretical and starts becoming real.

▪️ The future you paint should be bigger than your product. 

It should make investors feel that change is inevitable.

Inside the 22nd Century Frontier article, you'll find answers to questions like:

→ Why do so many good startup decks fail?

→ How do you make investors care before you talk about your product?

→ What's the simplest storytelling framework for fundraising?

→ How do you turn traction into a compelling narrative?

→ Why is clarity one of the biggest fundraising advantages?

If you're building a deck, fundraising, or helping founders tell better stories, this one is worth your time.

sections.title: How it works — Collaboration process
sections.body:
Step 1 | Submission
Select your preferred collaboration format and submit your request. If any details are missing or require refinement, I will follow up with questions to ensure strategic alignment.

Step 2 | Review and confirmation
Each request is carefully evaluated for audience fit and performance potential. If approved, you will receive a confirmation along with a secure payment link. If not, I may suggest a more effective alternative.

Step 3 | Payment
Production begins immediately once payment is completed.

Step 4 | Content development
Based on the collaboration type, you may provide creative assets and copy, or I will handle concept development, writing, and visual or video production.

Step 5 | Approval and scheduling
You review the final draft and creative. Once approved, you can specify your preferred publication timing for launch day.

Step 6 | Publication and reporting
Your campaign goes live as scheduled. Afterward, you receive performance insights and engagement metrics.
